definitions.explanation: Glasses used to correct age-related farsightedness (presbyopia). Typically used by people in their 40s and older who have difficulty reading small text up close.

examples.japanese: {老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}をかける。
{最近|さいきん}、{老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}がないと{新聞|しんぶん}が{読|よ}めない。
examples.english: Lately I can't read the newspaper without reading glasses.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{四十代|よんじゅうだい}で{老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}を{使|つか}い{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: My father started using reading glasses in his forties.

notes:
Glasses specifically designed to correct {老眼|ろうがん} (presbyopia), the age-related difficulty in focusing on nearby objects.

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {老眼|ろうがん} (presbyopia) + {鏡|きょう} (lens/glasses).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}をかける: to put on reading glasses
- {老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}を{外|はず}す: to take off reading glasses
- {老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう}が{必要|ひつよう}になる: to start needing reading glasses

ALTERNATIVE EXPRESSIONS:
Some people avoid {老眼鏡|ろうがんきょう} because the character {老|ろう} (old) feels blunt. Softer alternatives include:
- リーディンググラス: "reading glasses" (loanword)
- {手元用|てもとよう}メガネ: glasses for close-up use

RELATED WORDS:
- メガネ / {眼鏡|めがね}: glasses (general)
- {遠近両用|えんきんりょうよう}メガネ: bifocal/progressive glasses
